question: Does pre-pretraining a language-model backbone on multi-step formal derivations accelerate later natural-language skill acquisition more than Dyck-language or procedural warmups, reorganize its internal geometry, and make the final model more robust to unstructured weight pruning?

key_findings.claim: Logic-PPT turns a diverse rule library into next-step proof supervision while transferring only the symbolic model's Transformer backbone into language pretraining.
key_findings.evidence: The library contains 247 schemata: 49 propositional, 77 term-logic, and 121 first-order rules. Backward chaining builds trees up to ten expansions, five injective symbol-renaming variants preserve structure, and post-order traversal yields valid forward derivations. Six million examples expose the model to 2.600B character-level logic tokens; the logic embedding and head are then discarded and the backbone receives a new Mistral-tokenizer embedding and language head.

key_findings.claim: All symbolic warmups yield a small persistent language-modeling advantage, but perplexity barely distinguishes logic from simpler symbolic data.
key_findings.evidence: After 108.6B natural-language tokens, the random-initialization baseline has FineWeb-Edu perplexity 11.183, compared with 11.088 for algorithmic PPT and 11.074 for both formal-language and logic PPT. Logic-PPT opens its gap in the first billion tokens, but its final perplexity improvement over the baseline is only 0.97% and is tied with the Dyck-based condition.

key_findings.claim: On the selected elemental linguistic tasks, logic derivations accelerate threshold crossing and finish substantially ahead of the other initialization conditions.
key_findings.evidence: Logic-PPT reaches 80% mean accuracy with 36B fewer natural-language tokens than ordinary pretraining. At the final checkpoint, mean accuracy over 17 selected tasks is 87.4%, versus 80.3% for formal-language PPT, 77.3% for ordinary pretraining, and 76.8% for algorithmic PPT. Its strongest category gains over the best alternative are 5.5-6.7 percentage points in morphology, reading comprehension, and compositional tasks.

key_findings.claim: BLiMP does not support a uniquely strong logic advantage at this scale.
key_findings.evidence: All four conditions reach about 80% BLiMP accuracy within 10-25B tokens and then plateau for the remaining 80B-plus tokens. Formal-language PPT is slightly best, while Logic-PPT is described as competitive and better than ordinary pretraining, motivating the authors' reliance on the more selective elemental-task suite for their main skill-emergence claim.

key_findings.claim: Logic pre-pretraining leaves a persistent and more sharply layered activation organization after 100B-plus language tokens.
key_findings.evidence: Self-layer CKA evolves from broadly similar layers into block-diagonal stages for every model, but Logic-PPT has the clearest blocks and lower similarity at boundaries. At the final checkpoint, its middle layers 4-9 are less similar to ordinary pretraining than the other PPT conditions, consistent with a distinct organization rather than simple convergence to the same representation.

key_findings.claim: The logic condition becomes more spectrally concentrated during the compression-seeking phase of natural-language training.
key_findings.evidence: Across middle and upper layers, Logic-PPT attains the lowest RankMe and highest fitted covariance spectral-decay rate later in training, indicating variance concentrated along fewer activation directions. The authors interpret this as compact organization rather than collapse, supported by higher task accuracy, but the metrics themselves do not establish causal efficiency.

key_findings.claim: Formal derivation training produces a distinctive continued contraction of attention and MLP weight spectra during the symbolic stage.
key_findings.evidence: All symbolic PPT conditions start natural-language training with lower attention-matrix stable rank than the ordinary baseline. During symbolic pre-pretraining, Logic-PPT stable rank continues falling across attention and MLP matrices, while formal-language and algorithmic conditions fall early and then plateau.

key_findings.claim: The Logic-PPT endpoint is markedly more resilient to Wanda pruning on the evaluated language and skill metrics.
key_findings.evidence: At 40% unstructured sparsity, Logic-PPT mean elemental-task accuracy drops from 0.87 to 0.745, a 14.4% relative decline, compared with 24.7% for ordinary pretraining, 22.0% for formal-language PPT, and 31.6% for algorithmic PPT. It also has the smallest FineWeb-Edu perplexity increase, and around 33% sparsity it matches the dense ordinary baseline's accuracy.

key_findings.claim: The only multi-seed check supports early CKA-pattern stability, not the full 100B behavioral or pruning claims.
key_findings.evidence: Three transferred-model seeds are trained for 10B natural-language tokens. Their self-layer CKA vectors have mean pairwise Pearson correlations of 0.9926 for Logic-PPT and above 0.99 for every condition, with small absolute differences. The authors explicitly state that each primary 100B condition is a single run.

method.core_idea: Warm up a randomly initialized Transformer on structurally rich symbolic proofs rather than raw text, discard all vocabulary-specific parameters, and test whether the retained backbone changes the speed, geometry, and compressibility of a long subsequent language-pretraining trajectory.
method.mechanism: Curate propositional, Aristotelian term-logic, and first-order inference schemata. Sample a goal, backward-chain applicable rules into a derivation tree, rename symbols injectively to create variants, traverse the tree post-order, and train next-step proof prediction with loss only on the target step. Compare this 2.600B-token Logic-PPT stage against token-matched Dyck/Shuffle-Dyck and set/sort/union warmups. Reinitialize embeddings and output heads, then train every 254M-parameter Qwen3-14L model on about 100B FineWeb-Edu tokens. Save dense checkpoints; evaluate held-out perplexity, BLiMP, a selected 17-task elemental suite, activation CKA, RankMe, covariance spectral decay, weight stable rank, and Wanda pruning up to 40% sparsity.
assumptions: The curated formal derivations exercise variable binding, quantifier scope, relation composition, and long-range dependencies that transfer to natural language.
Discarding the symbolic embedding and head isolates useful structure in the shared Transformer backbone.
Approximately matching observed PPT token counts is a fair comparison despite different tokenizers, sequence lengths, loss positions, learning rates, weight decay, and checkpoint steps.
The selected 17 elemental tasks reflect general skill acquisition rather than a post hoc subset favorable to Logic-PPT.
Lower RankMe, faster spectral decay, and lower stable rank indicate efficient organization rather than harmful representational collapse.
Wanda pruning under the chosen calibration and sparsity setup is a meaningful test of model compressibility.
One 100B-token run per condition is sufficiently representative for the main ordering, with 10B CKA seed checks serving as partial support.
Behavior at 254M parameters extrapolates to larger language models and broader post-training regimes.

techniques.role: Builds valid multi-step derivations by recursively unifying rule conclusions with current tree leaves.
Creates surface-diverse proofs while holding topology and inference-rule sequence fixed.
Converts a backward-built tree into valid leaf-to-root forward prefixes and trains only the next derived formula.
Removes the character vocabulary and logic head so subsequent effects must pass through Transformer blocks.
Tracks behavior and representation geometry throughout more than 100B natural-language tokens instead of only at the endpoint.
Measures within-model stage differentiation and between-model persistence of PPT-induced activation structure.
Uses entropy effective rank and power-law decay to monitor expansion then concentration of representational variance.
Measures how attention and MLP singular-value energy concentrates during symbolic and language training.
Prunes weights using magnitude times input-channel activation norm to test whether the induced organization survives sparsity.

evaluations.setting: Four 254M-parameter Qwen3-14L models trained from scratch on approximately 108.6B FineWeb-Edu tokens after zero or approximately 2.6B symbolic tokens
evaluations.baseline: Randomly initialized ordinary pretraining and token-matched algorithmic/formal-language PPT

evaluations.setting: Seventeen elemental tasks selected because at least one PPT condition reaches 80% within the training budget
evaluations.metric: Mean accuracy trajectory and tokens needed to reach 80%
evaluations.result: Logic-PPT finishes at 87.4% and reaches 80% with 36B fewer natural-language tokens; Formal-PPT 80.3%, PT 77.3%, Alg-PPT 76.8% at the endpoint

evaluations.setting: BLiMP linguistic minimal pairs over the 100B-token trajectory
evaluations.result: All models reach about 80% within 10-25B tokens and remain close; Formal-PPT is slightly strongest

evaluations.setting: Fifteen-thousand held-out FineWeb-Edu examples at multiple checkpoints
evaluations.metric: Self and pairwise layer CKA, RankMe, and fitted eigenspectrum decay
evaluations.result: Logic-PPT shows clearer layer blocks, lower middle-layer similarity to PT, lower late RankMe, and faster spectral decay in middle/upper layers
evaluations.baseline: The same metrics for PT, Formal-PPT, and Alg-PPT

evaluations.setting: Attention and MLP weights during symbolic PPT and later language pretraining
evaluations.result: Logic-PPT continues contracting through its symbolic stage while other PPT spectra plateau early; all PPT attention matrices begin language training below PT
evaluations.baseline: Formal-language, algorithmic, and ordinary pretraining weight trajectories

evaluations.setting: Unstructured Wanda pruning through 40% sparsity at the final checkpoint
evaluations.metric: Mean elemental-task accuracy and FineWeb-Edu perplexity
evaluations.result: At 40%, Logic-PPT loses 14.4% relative task accuracy versus 22.0-31.6% for alternatives and has the smallest perplexity increase; near 33% it matches dense PT task accuracy
evaluations.baseline: Dense and equivalently pruned PT, Formal-PPT, and Alg-PPT models

evaluations.setting: Three reinitializations per transferred backbone trained for 10B natural-language tokens
evaluations.metric: Pairwise self-layer CKA matrix difference and correlation
evaluations.result: Mean Pearson correlation exceeds 0.99 for every condition; Logic-PPT is 0.9926 with mean absolute difference 0.0182
evaluations.baseline: Cross-seed variation within each initialization condition

limitations: Author-stated: all main behavioral, mechanistic, and pruning findings come from one 100B-token run for each condition; only 10B CKA organization is checked over three seeds.
Author-stated: the study uses one approximately 254M-parameter architecture, so neither model-scale laws nor larger-model persistence are established.

Author-stated: evaluation emphasizes pretraining acquisition, BLiMP, elemental tasks, geometry, and pruning; it does not test supervised fine-tuning, instruction following, broad question answering, or natural-language reasoning transfer.
Author-stated: the study is primarily English and does not establish transfer across languages with different morphology, syntax, and writing systems.
Author-stated: PPT conditions are only approximately token-matched, with task-specific sequence lengths and configurations inherited from prior work.

Reviewer-identified: the three symbolic baselines also differ in tokenizer vocabulary, maximum sequence length (2048 versus 128), learning rate, weight decay, loss positions, sampling, and number of training examples, so logic content is confounded with optimization and context regime.

Reviewer-identified: the main 17-task mean is selected after observing that at least one PPT model crosses 80%; full 130-task curves are supplied, but no aggregate full-suite headline quantifies whether the advantage survives the selection rule.

Reviewer-identified: the 36B figure counts natural-language tokens but Logic-PPT consumes an extra 2.6B symbolic tokens and associated compute, which should be included in end-to-end efficiency comparisons.

Reviewer-identified: lower effective rank and stronger spectral concentration correlate with pruning resilience but do not establish that the geometry causes either skill acceleration or compressibility.

Reviewer-identified: pruning is tested with one unstructured method and no latency, memory-bandwidth, recovery fine-tuning, or structured-sparsity measurement, limiting claims about deployable compression.

Reviewer-identified: concurrent evidence reports that formal-language PPT gains can depend strongly on seed, tokenizer, model size, and target language, making the single-run behavioral ordering especially uncertain.
failure_modes: The proof generator produces surface-diverse but topologically repetitive derivations, allowing rule-sequence templates rather than abstract logic to dominate learning.
Formal notation biases attention toward rare character-level patterns that do not transfer when natural-language structure differs from the curated proof schemas.
The symbolic phase is too long and over-specializes the backbone, creating negative transfer for skills such as those where Alg-PPT underperforms ordinary pretraining.
An apparent speedup disappears when total symbolic-plus-language tokens or total FLOPs are matched.
A different initialization seed, tokenizer, or target language reverses the PPT ordering.
Low-rank concentration becomes representational collapse at larger scale or on tasks needing many independent features.
Wanda's activation-weighted score happens to align with Logic-PPT spectra, but structured pruning or quantization does not preserve the advantage.
Post-training overwrites or bypasses the initialization-induced organization, eliminating the pretraining skill and compression gains.
reusable_insights: When transferring across disjoint vocabularies, reset embeddings and output heads to isolate what the shared backbone learned.
Generate proof trees backward for controllability, then serialize them post-order so every supervised next step is valid from the visible prefix.
Use injective symbol renaming to separate structural transfer from memorization of particular predicates or variables.
Track long training trajectories because small early loss gaps and later capability gaps can persist even when endpoint perplexity nearly ties.
Pair spectral diagnostics with a concrete intervention such as pruning; geometry is more useful when it predicts an operational outcome.
Match total compute, tokenizer, context length, optimizer, and loss positions when comparing symbolic curricula, not only observed token counts.
Report both pre-specified broad suites and emergence-filtered subsets so threshold analyses do not become selection-biased.
Replicate at least a shorter proxy run across seeds before investing in one very long trajectory, then confirm key behavioral findings at full scale.
open_questions: Does Logic-PPT retain its behavioral advantage across full-scale seeds once the CKA check is extended beyond 10B tokens?
Which component—multi-step depth, variable binding, quantification, relation composition, or simply long context—causes the transfer?
Does the result survive a factorial comparison with identical tokenizer, sequence length, optimizer, loss masking, and total FLOPs?
How does Logic-PPT scale from 254M to multi-billion-parameter models, and does its value shrink or grow with language-data budget?
Do the gains persist through instruction tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, and broad reasoning evaluation?
Can activation or weight spectral changes prospectively predict which symbolic curriculum will improve a new target language or skill?
Is Logic-PPT also more robust to quantization, structured pruning, layer dropping, and low-rank factorization under real hardware metrics?
Would multilingual or natural-language-rendered proofs transfer more broadly than character-level formal formulas?
Can controlled ablations of the 247-rule library reveal a minimal curriculum with a better total-compute return?

competitive_landscape.title: Between Circuits and Chomsky: Pre-pretraining on Formal Languages Imparts Linguistic Biases
competitive_landscape.difference: Hu et al. establish formal-language pre-pretraining, report up to 33% natural-language token savings for a 1B model, and causally track transferred attention heads. Logic-PPT replaces Dyck-style dependency primitives with propositional, term, and first-order derivations, extends language training to about 100B tokens, analyzes activation and weight spectra, and adds pruning resilience, but uses a smaller model and only one full-run seed.

competitive_landscape.title: Procedural Pretraining: Warming Up Language Models with Abstract Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Jiang et al. broaden PPT to formal languages plus set, sort, and union procedures, test models up to 1.3B, and report target-loss attainment with 55-86% of the original natural-language data. Logic-PPT uses their procedural mixture as a direct baseline and argues that richer formal derivations yield stronger selected linguistic skills and a distinct compact geometry, while adding a 100B-token trajectory and pruning intervention.

competitive_landscape.title: Synthetic Pre-Pre-Training Improves Language Model Robustness to Noisy Pre-Training Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Guo et al. use only 65M structured synthetic tokens to make a 1B model resist corrupted pretraining text, attaining the same final loss with up to 49% fewer natural tokens and analyzing attention to noise. Logic-PPT spends about 2.6B proof tokens and targets clean-data skill acquisition plus pruning, with richer derivations but no noisy-corpus robustness evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Instability of LLM Pre-Pretraining: It Doesn't Always Help. An Investigation on Multiple Languages
competitive_landscape.difference: Riazhskykh et al. test formal-language PPT across four language families, two tokenizers, model sizes, and seeds, finding gains highly setup- and seed-dependent despite some stable Dyck benefits. That concurrent result directly challenges the external validity of Logic-PPT's single-seed English behavioral ranking and raises the priority of multi-seed, tokenizer-matched replication.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: Logic-PPT is the first use of structurally rich formal derivations as a pre-pretraining curriculum, the first 100B-token study of its persistent behavioral and geometric effects, and the first demonstration that PPT-induced organization improves pruning resilience. Formal-language and procedural pre-pretraining, smaller-scale token-efficiency gains, backbone-transfer mechanisms, and logic-data synthesis all predate it. Reviewer inference: the strongest novelty is the combined experiment—247-rule multi-family derivations, a long clean-language trajectory, spectral and CKA diagnostics, and an operational Wanda-pruning test. The reported 87.4% selected-task endpoint and 14.4% pruning drop are promising, but one full seed, post hoc task selection, materially mismatched PPT configurations, and a concurrent instability study prevent a firm claim that logic itself is the causal or generally superior curriculum.
reviewer_notes: All 29 pages were checked, including formal definitions, synthesis and transfer procedure, behavioral curves, mechanism metrics, pruning results, author limitations, architecture and optimizer tables, derivation-generation details, CKA seed check, all logic samples, PPT configuration table, full task-suite figures, and BLiMP breakdown. The full 130-task suite is plotted but the quantitative 87.4% headline is for the filtered 17-task subset. Competitive titles, identifiers, and scopes were verified on primary arXiv records current through 2026-08-23, including the concurrent multilingual instability result.
